game.title: Martian Outpost

settings.window_resolution_hint: Fullscreen uses your monitor size. The selected resolution applies when you return to windowed mode.

setup.select_crew.required: Select exactly four astronauts to start.

onboarding.built: Building complete! Select it on the map to inspect it.
onboarding.help: The guide checks your actions. Closing a message does not complete a task. You can skip it without losing your mission.
onboarding.reassign.body: Research needs more working hours. Return to Laboratory and assign 8 hours to two free people; a completed task no longer adds work. Then press Resume.
onboarding.no_lab.body: There is no working laboratory. Rebuild one beside a tunnel and check its power. If you need plates, salvage an available rocket to recover 12. The guide will wait; you can use any panel.
onboarding.no_budget.body: You still need materials for this building. Save what remains. Salvaging an available rocket gives 12 plates and one chip; you cannot salvage a rocket already used for crew exchange. Open Rocket to plan the next arrival.
onboarding.breach.body: A leak! Pause and choose Focus. In the tunnel inspector, Isolate stops oxygen loss but disconnects this segment. Then assign a repair and resume so the crew member can work.
onboarding.repair.body: The leak is isolated. Now choose a free person and Repair: “Use spare parts” consumes one. Press Resume to do the work. The segment reconnects after completion, not just after you issue the order.
onboarding.dust.body: Dust is coming: solar generation will drop. In the panel inspector, enable Protect. This prevents dust buildup but does not remove the storm’s loss of sunlight. Watch Energy and battery charge.
onboarding.flare.body: Radiation is coming. In Crew, choose Shelter for each person. Outdoor tasks stop while sheltered. When the flare ends, choose Leave shelter to resume outdoor work.
onboarding.refuel.body: The reactor is low on fuel. You have a core: choose Focus, select a free person and Refuel. Then resume to complete the work. A core in inventory does not refuel the reactor on its own.
onboarding.no_core.body: The reactor is low on fuel and you have no core. Request one on the next rocket and prepare your battery and solar panel. After arrival, assign Refuel in the reactor inspector.
onboarding.scan.body: To explore, unlock Satellite scan and choose a sector beside revealed land. Scanning costs 6 stored energy and 8 research points, in addition to unlocking the technology.
onboarding.welcome.title: Let’s learn together!
onboarding.welcome.body: I’m your guide robot. Keep the colony alive for 42 sols. Choose “Learn with me”: we’ll pause to explain each goal. You can also play without the guide.
onboarding.supplies.title: Keep your colony alive
onboarding.supplies.body: Look at the top bar: oxygen, water and food are supplies. Your crew uses them; the ISRU and greenhouse produce more when powered. Open Resources to see the amounts.
onboarding.energy.title: Power before expansion
onboarding.energy.body: In Energy, compare generation and demand. The starting reactor powers the colony plus a laboratory, but its fuel lasts 14 sols. Keep it on. We’ll add solar power before spending on more buildings.
onboarding.tunnel.title: Connect a tunnel
onboarding.tunnel.body: Open Build and choose Tunnel. Place one beside the base: the marked cell is a safe option. Green means valid; red means something is missing or blocked. Right-click cancels placement.
onboarding.laboratory.title: Build your laboratory
onboarding.laboratory.body: Now place a Laboratory beside the tunnel. It costs 16 plates and one chip. “Show goal” prepares a safe location; you choose when to build. Buildings cannot share occupied cells.
onboarding.solar_research.title: Choose a discovery
onboarding.solar_research.body: Open Laboratory, select Solar panel and press Research. Choosing a technology does not advance its bar: people must work on it too. If the button is disabled, check power and any ongoing research.
onboarding.solar_workers.title: Assign working hours
onboarding.solar_workers.body: In Laboratory, keep 8 hours, choose a free crew member and press Assign research work. Repeat with another person. The panel needs 12 working hours: one order for 8 hours is not enough.
onboarding.solar_wait.title: Let time move
onboarding.solar_wait.body: Press Resume or Space. Your crew will work and the bar will rise. Pause whenever you want; ×1 is comfortable for learning. I’ll tell you when the panel unlocks. Working hours are not sols.
onboarding.solar_panel.title: Build your discovery
onboarding.solar_panel.body: Solar panel unlocked! Open Build and place one in the marked area. Research unlocks the building; construction still costs materials. You’ll have 5 plates left if you followed this route.
onboarding.day_night_ready.body: Panels produce much less at night. Batteries charge only from surplus power, then help cover demand. Open Energy and distinguish generation, capacity and stored charge.
onboarding.day_night.title: Solar power drops at night
onboarding.day_night.body: Panels produce much less at night and during storms. A battery stores power, but costs 8 plates: we cannot afford it yet. Keep the remaining 5 plates; the first rocket will help.
onboarding.landing_zone.title: Reserve a rocket landing site
onboarding.landing_zone.body: Open Rocket and select Rocket 1. Reserve a clear 8×8 square: X=22, Y=22 is a safe starting option. Keep that area clear. Arrival is scheduled for sol 7.
onboarding.rocket_manifest.title: Request useful supplies
onboarding.rocket_manifest.body: Add 1 nuclear core, 1 spare part and 1 seed to the cargo; they fit the mass limit. Press Confirm cargo. The core will refuel the reactor: storing it does not refuel the reactor automatically.
onboarding.rocket_arrival.title: Until the first rocket arrives
onboarding.rocket_arrival.body: Resume to reach sol 7. Watch supplies and check Report. You can try ×2, then return to ×1. If a leak appears, pause and handle its alert. You don’t need Demo or more construction.
onboarding.salvage.title: Recover rocket materials
onboarding.salvage.body: The rocket has arrived! In Rocket, choose an available crew member and Salvage. You’ll recover 12 plates and one chip. Salvaging and exchanging crew are mutually exclusive for that rocket.
onboarding.battery_research.title: Research a battery
onboarding.battery_research.body: Recovered materials let us plan a battery. In Laboratory, choose Battery and press Research. Finish any other ongoing research first. This discovery needs 14 working hours.
onboarding.battery_workers.title: Organize more research
onboarding.battery_workers.body: Assign 8 hours to two free crew members, as before. Check that they are not busy or sheltered. Schedules and priorities affect how long work takes; you do not need to change sleep hours to learn.
onboarding.battery_wait.title: Watch the progress
onboarding.battery_wait.body: Resume to complete Battery research. If the bar stops, check power and research orders with working hours remaining. You can return to Laboratory without losing progress.
onboarding.battery.title: Store energy for the night
onboarding.battery.body: Build a Battery near the marked solar panel. It costs 8 plates and one chip. It charges from surplus power; it does not generate power. Check capacity and charge in Energy.
onboarding.finish.title: You know the basic loop!
onboarding.finish.body: Build, research, assign work and watch your supplies. Prepare before every rocket. Watch the reactor’s fuel: refuel before it runs out. You can find this guide again in Help. The colony is yours to lead!
tutorial.first_night.title: Night is coming
tutorial.first_night.body: Solar generation falls at night. Watch power and battery reserves.
tutorial.lab.title: Research begins here
tutorial.lab.body: Build a Laboratory to research new technology.
tutorial.solar.title: Reliable power
tutorial.solar.body: You can now build a solar panel! Next, research batteries to store energy.
tutorial.scan.title: Search from orbit
tutorial.scan.body: Scan an adjacent sector to reveal aquifers and mineable ground.
tutorial.rocket.title: Prepare the rocket
tutorial.rocket.body: Choose cargo within the mass limit, then reserve a clear 8×8 landing zone.
tutorial.radiation.title: Radiation warning
tutorial.radiation.body: Keep the crew in the Base during the flare unless an outside emergency is worth the dose.
dialogue.tutorial_skipped: Tutorial skipped. You can re-enable it in Settings.

science.source.donki.explanation: NASA DONKI records solar activity such as flares and energetic particles. This game uses selected archived events to explain radiation warnings.
science.source.donki.limit: An archived event helps explain risk, but it is not a live Mars forecast and does not directly set health outcomes.
science.source.radlab.explanation: NASA's RadLab provides radiation measurements from instruments in space. It helps explain what a radiation dose means.
science.source.radlab.limit: These measurements are not Mars-surface readings, so the game does not treat them as a Mars dose.
science.source.mars_trek.explanation: NASA Mars Trek shares maps and terrain data from Mars missions. It inspires the outpost's terrain context.
science.source.mars_trek.limit: The game map is a simplified learning map, not a surveyed real landing site.
ambient.thought.1: The red horizon makes Earth feel very far away.
ambient.thought.2: A quiet greenhouse is the closest thing to a garden on Mars.
ambient.science.1: Mars has a thin atmosphere, so it cannot retain heat as well as Earth.
ambient.science.2: Martian regolith is useful for shielding, but it is not soil for crops.

credits.link_failed: The link could not be opened. You can use the address shown on the card.
credits.science_intro: References used for the 3D buildings: studies, concepts and prototypes. Each card explains what its source supports and what our artist adapted.
credits.science_note: Checked on 15 Nov 2026. These are official NASA sources or works hosted in its NTRS repository; not all are authored by NASA. There is no single approved blueprint for this colony. Game geometry, costs and yields are adaptations.
credits.habitat.title: Central habitat · Protected modules
credits.habitat.fact: Study: Hexamars-2 proposes six partially buried spherical modules for a Martian habitat.
credits.habitat.limit: Our model: four modules around a central one. This arrangement is an artistic adaptation, not a NASA-approved blueprint.
credits.laboratory.title: Laboratory · Pressurized spaces
credits.laboratory.fact: Proposal: Inflatable Habitat Structure describes a horizontal cylindrical habitat for living and working on the Moon or Mars.
credits.laboratory.limit: Our model: three modules in a Y layout with a central body. The source supports the cylindrical concept, not this layout or its regolith cover.
credits.solar_model.title: Solar panels · Deploy to collect light
credits.solar_model.fact: Study: CTSA proposes a lightweight, deployable solar array for power on the surface of Mars.
credits.solar_model.limit: Our model: six panels around a support. Their number and shape are artistic choices; folding them does not guarantee protection from every storm.
credits.reactor_model.title: Reactor · Electricity and heat
credits.reactor_model.fact: Research: Fission Surface Power studies fission energy for planetary surfaces. The reference design in the TDU report includes radiators to reject heat.
credits.reactor_model.limit: Our model: a buried reactor and dish-shaped radiators. These are adaptations; radiators need exposed surfaces to dissipate heat. The 14-sol core is a game rule.
credits.isru_model.title: ISRU plant · Use Martian resources
credits.isru_model.fact: Study: a conceptual plant obtains water from ice and processes atmospheric CO₂ to produce methane and oxygen, with processing and storage equipment.
credits.isru_model.limit: Our model: a factory with tanks and an extraction tower. The tower is conceptual; extraction requires specific technology. The game simplifies this plant to water and oxygen production.
credits.refinery_model.title: Refinery · Process minerals
credits.refinery_model.fact: Research: a report hosted in NASA NTRS studies thermal processing of simulated Martian soil and the interest in obtaining materials such as iron and silicon.
credits.refinery_model.limit: Our model: a furnace, tanks and loading area. The layout and iron plate recipe are adaptations; simulant experiments do not demonstrate a refinery operating on Mars.
credits.mine_model.title: Mine · RASSOR robotic excavation
credits.mine_model.fact: Technology: RASSOR uses counterrotating excavation drums to reduce reaction forces while collecting regolith in low gravity.
credits.mine_model.limit: Our model: robots in an iron mine. RASSOR supports the digging mechanism; it does not establish an exploitable iron deposit at the game location.
credits.greenhouse_model.title: Greenhouse · Grow under protection
credits.greenhouse_model.fact: Study: Preliminary greenhouse design proposes three pressurized underground crop modules with thermal and radiation protection. NASA also describes greenhouse prototypes for exploration.
credits.greenhouse_model.limit: Our model: a large outer oval and three more deeply buried cylinders. The oval is an artistic choice; these proposals are not greenhouses already operating on Mars.
credits.battery_model.title: Batteries · Manage temperature
credits.battery_model.fact: Study: Heat Rejection Trade Study compares technologies for rejecting heat from systems intended for lunar and Martian surfaces.
credits.battery_model.limit: Our model: a battery container with thermal control. The connection is partial: the study does not prescribe this battery or its rectangular shape. Capacity and charging are game values.
credits.landing_model.title: Landing pad · Prepare for arrival
credits.landing_model.fact: Research: NASA studies grading and stabilizing regolith to reduce dust, rocks and debris thrown up by engine plumes during landing.
credits.landing_model.limit: Our model: a hardened landing area. Ground preparation is supported; specific dimensions, strength and materials require engineering and testing.
credits.tunnel_model.title: Tunnels · Travel with breathable air
credits.tunnel_model.fact: Concept: the University of Michigan team in M2M X-Hab studies pressurized tunnels to connect facilities and reduce spacewalks on Mars.
credits.tunnel_model.limit: Our model: cylindrical corridors between buildings. This is an academic reference hosted in NASA NTRS, not a built network or an officially approved NASA architecture.
learning.building.base.purpose: Colony centre: the crew lives here and can take shelter before a hazard.
learning.building.base.curiosity: Rounded shapes help withstand internal pressure. The reference habitat is a design study, not a base already built on Mars.
learning.building.isru.purpose: Produces water and oxygen with power and suitable ground.
learning.building.isru.curiosity: ISRU means using local resources. Studies combine Martian ice and CO₂ to obtain useful products instead of carrying everything from Earth.
learning.building.greenhouse.purpose: Grows crew food. It needs power; plants wilt without it.
learning.building.greenhouse.curiosity: A space greenhouse must control air, water, temperature and light. The cited study proposes crops in protected underground modules.
learning.building.laboratory.purpose: Enables technology research. Choose a project and assign enough work hours.
learning.building.laboratory.curiosity: Scientists need pressurized spaces to work without suits. Our laboratory layout is an artistic adaptation.
learning.building.solar_panel.purpose: Converts light to electricity. Dust reduces output; check protection and cleaning.
learning.building.solar_panel.curiosity: Deployable arrays take less space during transport. The CTSA concept studies deploying a large solar surface on Mars.
learning.building.battery.purpose: Stores spare energy and supplies it when generation cannot cover demand. It does not create electricity.
learning.building.battery.curiosity: Temperature matters: surface equipment must reject heat. A full battery also needs charge and discharge limits.
learning.building.reactor.purpose: Generates electricity day and night while fuel lasts. Refuel it in time.
learning.building.reactor.curiosity: A reactor produces heat and converts it to electricity. Its radiators reject waste heat and need exposed surfaces.
learning.building.mine.purpose: Extracts ore and regolith from a deposit. It needs power and mineral ground.
learning.building.mine.curiosity: RASSOR uses counterrotating drums to excavate without relying as much on robot weight in low gravity.
learning.building.refinery.purpose: Turns ore into iron plates for construction. Watch its inputs and power.
learning.building.refinery.curiosity: Reference experiments heated simulated Martian soil. A simulant allows Earth-based research but does not demonstrate a factory operating on Mars.
learning.building.printer_3d.purpose: Makes spare parts and suits using game recipes. It consumes materials and power.
learning.building.printer_3d.curiosity: Plastic parts were printed layer by layer on the space station, including a wrench designed on Earth. Not every material or device can be printed this way.
learning.building.landing_pad.purpose: Improves rocket cargo capacity. You still need to reserve and confirm its arrival zone.
learning.building.landing_pad.curiosity: Engines can throw up dust and rocks. NASA studies preparing the ground before landing to reduce that hazard.
learning.building.tunnel.purpose: Connects buildings. If it leaks, isolation stops the loss; it still needs repair.
learning.building.tunnel.curiosity: A corridor with air could allow travel between facilities without a spacewalk. The Michigan reference is an academic concept, not a built network on Mars.
learning.event.dust_storm.title: Dust storm
learning.event.dust_storm.why: The Sun heats the ground unevenly. This moves the air; winds and vortices can lift Martian dust.
learning.event.dust_storm.consequence: Dust blocks some sunlight and settles on panels. In the game, electricity falls: equipment can shut down, water or oxygen can run short, and crops can wilt.
learning.event.dust_storm.response: Beforehand: store energy and check the reactor. Protect panels if needed, remembering they will produce less. Afterwards: check dust and assign cleaning when safe.
learning.event.dust_storm.limit: Martian wind does not push like an Earth hurricane. Here the main dust hazard is power loss. Duration and losses are game rules.
learning.event.solar_flare.title: Solar activity and radiation
learning.event.solar_flare.why: The Sun can release energy when its magnetic fields change. A flare is a flash of radiation; other solar events can accelerate particles travelling through space.
learning.event.solar_flare.consequence: In the game, the event raises dose outside the habitat: more during a spacewalk, less in another building. High accumulated dose eventually harms health, even if a task is blocked.
learning.event.solar_flare.response: Use Crew → Shelter to return to the habitat and suspend work. Wait until the event ends before leaving. Medicine improves health but does not erase accumulated dose.
learning.event.solar_flare.limit: The game groups solar risk into one simplified event. A flare and a particle storm are different; real shielding reduces risk rather than guaranteeing immunity. Dose uses game units, not a medical calculation.
learning.event.tunnel_breach.title: Tunnel leak
learning.event.tunnel_breach.why: Small rock fragments travelling through space can puncture a pressurized structure. In this game event, a simulated impact damages a tunnel and air escapes.
learning.event.tunnel_breach.consequence: If ignored, oxygen reserves decrease. If they run out, the crew loses health. Isolating the section stops the leak but also cuts that connection.
learning.event.tunnel_breach.response: Press Focus, isolate the tunnel and assign a repair in its panel. Resume so the person can work. Avoid outside repairs during a solar warning if you can wait.
learning.event.tunnel_breach.limit: The source explains puncture risk in space structures. Impact timing, damage, leakage and Mars repair time belong to the game simulation.
hud.reserve_explanation: Reference bar: {sols} sols of reserves without new production. Oxygen includes active leaks. Not maximum storage capacity.
hud.energy_explanation: Generation / demand. The bar shows how much demand receives electricity. Battery shows stored energy / capacity.
hud.pressure_explanation: Simplified status: warns when a tunnel leak loses oxygen. Not a physical pressure measurement.
learning.printer.limit: Real printing needs appropriate processes and materials. Complete spare parts and suits from plates and chips are simplified game recipes.
crew.exposure.indoors: In another building · return to habitat during radiation
error.shelter_unavailable: The habitat is unavailable as a shelter.
learning.event.dust_storm.brief: Wind has lifted dust: less sunlight reaches the panels, reducing power. Without reserves, water, oxygen and food equipment can stop. Check batteries, reactor and panel protection.
learning.event.dust_storm.warning: Warning: begins in {sols} sols. Wind has lifted dust: less sunlight reaches the panels, reducing power. Without reserves, water, oxygen and food equipment can stop. Check batteries, reactor and panel protection.
learning.event.solar_flare.brief: The Sun is active. This event raises radiation outside the habitat; high dose harms health. Use Crew → Shelter to suspend tasks and return. Learn why it happens before leaving.
learning.event.solar_flare.warning: Warning: begins in {sols} sols. The Sun is active. This event raises radiation outside the habitat; high dose harms health. Use Crew → Shelter to suspend tasks and return. Learn why it happens before leaving.
learning.event.tunnel_breach.brief: A simulated impact opened a leak, losing oxygen. Focus and isolate the section, then assign a repair and resume. Without oxygen, the crew loses health.
learning.event.tunnel_breach.warning: Warning: begins in {sols} sols. A simulated impact opened a leak, losing oxygen. Focus and isolate the section, then assign a repair and resume. Without oxygen, the crew loses health.
